essential: Parents' fear of Europe and of unsuitable in-laws, ironized against Henry's apparent respectability. They consent to his studying a Civil Law that neither he nor they understood.
The Persia's November gale teaches more than university, and the 'tourist mathematics' joke about impressions versus education.

England as felt romance (Chester, Eaton Hall, Dickens alive), then the Black District as an uncomfortable unknown society he runs away from, with the Karl Marx foreshadowing kept as retrospective irony.
London as an insolent eighteenth-century city; the retrospective note on its shrinking fifty years later; Antwerp as purely sensual, mediaeval education.

Berlin: easy descent into beer-cellars, then a single Civil Law lecture shows the university is worse than Harvard. Keep the argument that Civil Law is useless without Common Law, and the mention of the Pandects.
German students do not take professors seriously, read Heine instead, and claim to be 'learning the language'.
The Sumner encounter and his cabman boast, then Apthorp's advice leading to three months in the Gymnasium Ober-tertia among boys of twelve or thirteen.
Context of Berlin and Prussia in 1858: provincial, with Germans themselves wanting to escape the system. Keep the 'smacked of Heine' irony.
The Gymnasium critique: memory-only training, no reason, foul unventilated air, window-opening rebuked, and the conclusion 'near an indictable nuisance'.

Beethoven: he declares he loathes it, then involuntarily follows a symphony, and concludes Beethoven must be overrated for being so easily followed. Note that Wagner was reached only near forty years later.
No other sense awoke: art, Kant/Hegel and Goethe stay closed. He insists to his father that Berlin is best, yet the April tramp reveals the nightmare.

title: BERLIN (1858-1859)

verbatim.text: came from time wasted; studies neglected; vices indulged; education reversed;--it came from the despised beer-garden and music-hall; and it was accidental, unintended, unforeseen.

verbatim.purpose: Central image of the Beethoven awakening.

verbatim.purpose: Closing resolution and cadence.

dependencies.other_evidence: as gay and brilliant in the terrors of lockjaw as she had been in the careless fun of 1859

essential: The Thuringen tramp collapses after one walk; the companions drive to Weimar after resting at Goethe's spot. All are unsure why they are in Germany, and Henry stays for fear of exhausting his father's patience.
Dresden as no better for education; the start of eighteen months of 'accidental education', explicitly compared to the Beethoven lesson.
His honest self-deception: he loved an eighteenth-century, disunited, unpractical Germany, now vanishing. Germany then was judged incapable of organized energy.
Napoleon III's war on Austria (the clerk measuring Milan to Dresden) poses the moral problem: his principles require doubtful allies and robbery; he asks when robbery and murder become virtue.
Sister Mrs. Kuhn (married to Charles Kuhn, hotly Italian) takes the reins. Keep her description, his giving the reins to a woman, and the general law.
Milan as an end attained rather than a means, passing Beethoven. Include the pleasure/pain equivalent remark.
The Stelvio crossing: Cacciatori, uncertainty, the barricade below the Ortler glacier with even Mrs. Kuhn gasping; the woman's charm wins passage to Mals. After this, Germany never regains its charm.
Second Dresden winter: social failure at the Frau Hofrathin's. 'There were no accidents in Dresden.' Tally: no profession, unfit for Europe or America.
He has become a mere tourist; his father was right; Charles Francis Adams is busy supporting Seward in 1860.
Letters to Charles printed in the Boston Courier as 'the nearest approach he had yet made to an intelligent act'.

Rome in May 1860: mediaeval, unrestored sorcery; resists any law of progress or sequence. Gibbon's Capitol passage leads him to sit on the Ara Coeli steps asking Why. Keep Browning at the guillotine shock, and 'Perhaps it meant nothing.'

Naples to Palermo as despatch-bearer via Chandler and Captain Palmer. Garibaldi in the red shirt, impervious and unreadable, framed as 'knowledge of one's ignorance of men'. Then Paris: disapproval permitting enjoyment, ending 'mixed emotions but no education'.
optional: The Goethe verse lines 'Warte nur! balde / Rubest du auch!' (can be paraphrased if the irony survives).
The Guelph/Ghibelline cave-dwellers sentences in para 7 (keep 'Better take sides first').
'The Initials' novel reference and fencing lessons.
Pumpelly/King Apaches sentence (paired with the King dependency; may cut both).
Para 15, on brothers and scientific education.
Para 23 roster (Story, Mommsen), keeping its last two sentences.
Para 27 Garibaldi 'Autobiography' detail; condense.
The Paris restaurant and actor catalogue (keep the gist of the taste acquired).
risks: Many retained episodes compete for 2,800 words; the Paris and German-illusion sections may need heavy compression.

essential: The return to Quincy: the father does not mock the Pandects but makes Henry private secretary for the Washington winter; the Wide-Awake torch procession whose air 'was not that of innocence'.
No one wanted or planned the Civil War.
Washington unchanged, a rude colony with little to secede from; the Union only a sentiment.
Everyone as ignorant as he (Sumner's Oxenstiern quote may be compressed). Southern planters as unbalanced and provincial: 'excess of power... held by inadequate hands'.
The North offers only one's own New England type, poised to a fault; Raymond named as a man of the world.
Hope narrows to Sumner and Seward. Sumner: dogmatism of the station, but warranted. The two senators' mutual antipathy, with the naive secretary courting both.

Seward portrait: macaw head and cigar; mask versus features indistinguishable; 'Henry Adams thought it charming'; the effect of unselfishness. Seward and C. F. Adams essentially alike; the Adamses subordinate local to national interests.
Strategy hinges on Virginia; concessions risk dividing the party; Seward's dinner remark.
Secretaries learn nothing; John Hay appears, recognized as a friend; Henry's secret correspondence and ballrooms yield nothing.
Winfield Scott is the only figure equal to the crisis; Lincoln seen once at the Inaugural Ball and judged as lacking force, a judgment flagged as one he 'would have lost' on.
Sumner privately denounces Mr. Adams and breaks with the family; the shock 'opened a chasm'; rebel defections, even Lee's, cost no pang, but Sumner's struck home.
Washington in March 1861: vultures of patronage, a cost of a million lives; return to Horace Gray's law office, 'education in treason' failed.
optional: The Quincy November/grasshopper autumn sentence.
'John Adams was better off in Philadelphia' line.
Central and Western names (Preston King, Davis, Lovejoy) and average Congressman/Senator remarks.
The Senate dogmatism gradations (Conkling/Malvolio).
Hildreth's hereditary treachery charge (keep the general point).
The Matthew Arnold 'two worlds' sentence.
risks: Para 21 'Friends are born, not made' could be cut for space but is useful; watch the verbatim budget.

essential: Lincoln names C. F. Adams Minister to England; Blackstone shelved again; Henry chosen as the son who could be spared. He did not then know that Sumner opposed the appointment; Henry thinks the secretary was more unfit than the chief.
A weak staff (Charley Wilson); April 13 the war bursts; regiments march; brother Charles at Fort Independence; Henry sails on the Niagara.

The Minister sails May 1 as an eighteenth-century adventurer like John Adams and John Quincy, leaving no friend in the Senate; the cabin-boy later feels it as betrayal. Cassius Clay aboard as a 'teacher'.
Henry learns to hold his tongue; landing May 13.

His mistaken belief in a friendly anti-slavery England, then recognition of Confederate belligerency on May 13. Nearly all England expected Davis to succeed; Palmerston 'prudently held his tongue'; Russell recognized before Adams arrived. These are the young man's perceptions.
Henry's dullness of comprehension; his unreflecting confidence in his father, whose composure was unmatched. The 'amhandheggsir' joke at Maurigy's Hotel.
Ironic luck: the blow passed over the Minister; Russell may have intended kindness; the Ministry was a little ashamed.
The son's position absurd: social ostracism, no help to give; secretaries uninterested, 'Quel chien de pays!'
Social torments: hiding at Burdett Coutts's, the Sutherland leap-frog, the forced Highland fling with the Duchess of Somerset.

Bull Run strengthens the Legation's resignation (three-month horizon); the gloom of December 1861; the Trent news cheered by the secretaries as war; the Minister at Fryston; the Prince Consort's death.
The Times satire on his Manchester letter ends 'usefulness'; Joe Parkes; obscurity saves him; 'Surtout point de zele!'; lasting grudge against the Times editor (Delane).

Mrs. Russell Sturgis at Mount Felix as the single warmth. British prejudice against Lincoln and Seward; the Minister slowly accepted as a sort of eminent counsel. Allies Milnes, Forster, Bright and Cobden, each briefly characterized. Argyll and the Mill-dinner anecdote; literary intimacies (Trevelyan, Lyells, Hughes). Closing: 'He meant to go home.'

The prize-fight metaphor elaboration; keep briefly.
